abstract.p: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems are designed to extract text from images. While typically optimised for modern documents, they often struggle when applied to historical documents due to older fonts, complex layouts, and physical degradation, which can result in noisy outputs. To reduce OCR errors, post-OCR algorithms are commonly used, however, their development and evaluation require image-transcription pairs. Compared to other European languages, there is a lack of transcribed documents for historical Portuguese, especially for texts predating the 19th century. To address this gap, we introduce Portuguese post-OCR Resources for Text Optimisation (PORTO), a dataset that spans from the 17th to the 20th centuries. PORTO contains 3,782 image-transcription pairs, along with OCR outputs from four different systems, providing a valuable resource for the development and evaluation of OCR and post-OCR methods tailored to historical Portuguese.
